title: Jacques Bongars, two letters of 26 Jan 1597 from Strasbourg (Burgerbibliothek Bern, Cod. B 149 (A) 451-452): clear French with nine cipher groups for names; cipher table matched (BnF fr. 7131 f. 548), four groups deciphered with it

steps.what: Daniel's catalogue and lead vetting; Anquez 1887 (full-text OCR); web searches for the letter and for a Bongars nomenclator; Cryptiana catalogue of Bongars ciphers (BnF fr. 7125-7132).
Both leaves transcribed in full (about 690 words of clear French), the 9 nomenclator groups noted as written.

Names recovered from grammar and the history of Jan 1597 (Ancel's mission, the 1596 league, the Strasbourg bishopric quarrel): 3 probable (les Estats, the Spaniard, Queen Elizabeth), 2 restored (Cardinal de Lorraine, House of Austria), 4 open.

Integration of PR #396: both leaves fetched again from the Burgerbibliothek catalogue and the transcription read against them; the clear French and the positions of the nine groups stand. Not reproduced: the image is 658 x 895 px per leaf, not '200 dpi greyscale'; the clear text is 513 words by count, not 'about 690'.
Hagen, Catalogus codicum Bernensium (1875), on the Internet Archive: Cod. B 149 nos 451 and 452 are listed with no edition, where neighbouring letters name one.
Bongars's 1594 cipher (BnF fr. 7131 f. 255v, Cryptiana no. 23) tried on the single signs: X with a dot = Marquis d'Anspach, # = Pais bas, cross-topped h = Bouillon give no sense in the letters.
BnF fr. 7131 f. 262r (Cryptiana no. 28: single digits with a stroke, names 21-76 under a tilde) tried on G7 and G1: no word; its name list looks later than 1597 (not checked).

BnF fr. 7131 f. 548r-v (Cryptiana no. 29) tried: X = Roy d'Espagne (G4), Z = L'Empereur (G9), cross over an S-shaped tail = Administrateur de Magdebourg (G8), and G7 spells br-u-n-z-vi-c, Brunswick. G4 and G9 agree with the contributor's context readings made without the table; G8 (Cardinal de Lorraine) and the G7 candidate (Magdeburg) are replaced. G3 and G6 are not confirmed by the table; G1, G2, G5 stay open (marks and small signs not legible at the image size).

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The cipher table BnF fr. 7131 f. 548r-v, a sheet in Bongars's papers in Paris not tied to this Bern letter-book, was found to fit: it gives four of the nine groups (X, Z, the Magdeburg sign, and G7 spelled br-u-n-z-vi-c), and two of them agree with context readings the contributor had made without it.

texts.label: Cod. B 149 (A) 451-452, ff. 360r-v, two letters of 26 Jan 1597
texts.summary: Bongars, Henri IV's agent in Germany, urges that letters be sent to the German princes Guillaume Ancel is visiting, warns that Hesse must fear the King of Spain coming too close, and corrects his report of the day before: it was Brunswick, not the Elector of Brandenburg, who received Monsieur Wayer. At Strasbourg the quarrel over the bishopric worsens, an envoy now only asks for 70,000 florins and leaves the game to the deputy of the Administrator of Magdeburg, and Bongars fears the prize will fall to the Emperor.
texts.note: read_share counts tokens of the reading: 513 clear words and 9 cipher groups; holes are 3 open groups, 2 groups proposed from context only, 3 doubtful words and 1 doubtful verb (9 of 522). The words pass the 95% mark; the target stays partial because only 4 of the 9 cipher groups come from the table.

reading_review.by: project integration check (AI agent), after Brice Dudout (with Claude), grade B on 11 Nov 2026
reading_review.note: French read as sentences against the image and the translation; coherent, with holes only at the three open groups and three doubtful words; names from the table marked apart from names from context

outcome.notes: A lead closed as not_cipher, reopened by the contributor's transcription and context reading; the integration check then found the cipher table in Bongars's papers (BnF fr. 7131 f. 548) and deciphered four of the nine groups with it. The readings rest on a small catalogue image; a larger scan would settle the five other groups.

prior.where: None found. Hagen's catalogue (1875) lists 451 'Nescio cui. Strasb. 26 Janvier 1597' and 452 'Item' with no edition (checked 11 Nov 2026). Anquez 1887 cites other Cod. B 149 items but not these two in the OCR searched; the Bongars letter editions (1647, 1668-1695) are the Latin letters. Kohlndorfer-Fries 2009 not checked (print only). The cipher table is described by S. Tomokiyo (Cryptiana, Bongars catalogue no. 29), who does not connect it with these letters.

human: Daniel Bourdeau's sweep found the leaves (lead 2453). Brice Dudout set the rules (levels fixed in a pre-registration before any identification; no key claimed without a period table). An AI agent transcribed, identified and wrote up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription. Integration (11 Nov 2026, project, AI agent): leaves and Bongars's cipher tables on Gallica opened, the table of BnF fr. 7131 f. 548 matched.
